It did not disappoint. The curry and the rice were all delicious. But my favourite was actually the mango chutney they give you. Finally we decided we will not continue any meals here as we were concerned and worried about our valuable guest and was not confident about ROBIN being and Indian treating our Indian guest so badly ,shame on Robin

Robin needs to change his attitude and behaviour as bad " Karmas" will need to be paid back here only

Generally Very Good Overall But Can Be A Bit Hit and Miss
Apr 2019 • Solo
Baba's D2 has super friendly attentive staff and is very close to my home which is why I have been there so often. Some of their dishes have been superb but depending on the chef the curries sometimes lack consistency. At its best their spicy curries are superb, for example their Vindaloo Chicken and Malibar Chicken and are at the same spiciness as are all Vindaloo curries world wide. But occasionally their curries are more like Phall than Vindaloos and far too spicy to eat. In fairness if this happens when I am in the restaurant the waiters notice and the chef cools down the curries to a regular Vindaloo hotness instead. It doesn't really help to ask for medium to spicy either as then the curries come somewhat mild. At their best, and at a regular Vindaloo spiciness, Baba's Vindaloo curries are the best anywhere and hence the 4 star rating. It's just a shame that the spiciness is dependent on individual chefs there as if the spicy curries were to a recognisable consistent spiciness then Baba's would definitely deserve a 5 star rating. Their vegetable samosas are very good, as is their pulao rice. Their french fries tend to be overcooked though thankfully not burned and their fried papadam massalas are delicious. I am hoping that the more times I go there that their spicy curries will become consistent as at their best , they really are very good.

reviews.review_text:
Manouph
Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam28 contributions

Impeccable service and good quality food
May 2019 • Family
We were a group of 3 people, going out for dinner to celebrate Mother's Day. After finishing dinner at a Mediterranean restaurant nearby, we walked along this bustling walking area to check out what it has to offer and came across this restaurant, which was actually relocated from a few houses away (if my memory does not fail me).

Im the past, the restaurant was quite small, but the food and service was good. This time, impressed by the new look - brighter and more spacious than the previous location - we decided to have round 2 of dinner! 

At first, we thought the price would be higher than the past since they would need to offset the cost of relocation. However, it is still reasonably priced, and the food quality cannot be complained.

We were welcomed with one complimentary dish, fried vegetables which can be dipped with some hot mango sauce (which tastes soooo good in my opinion). After taking ordered, the waiter quickly brought 3 cups of free plain water for us to drink while waiting (cuz it took a while for them to properly cook the food). He didnt fail to refill whenever seeing that we almost drank it up (which is a big plus point, as many restaurants do not do this though plain water does not cost that much!)

When we almost finished our meal, we were offered another complimentary rice pudding meant to cool down the heat we took in after eating all the hot food.

The average price range is about vnd120k-vnd140k/ a small pot of curry. Naan is about 50k, which I think is fair if you compare with other restaurants on Hai Ba Trung or Dong Du. Budget for one person eating here (and feel super full!) should be around vnd200k to 250k. Eating with a group is a good idea, cuz you get to try different kinds of curry if you share with the rest.

In summary, it is highly recommended.

PS: the restaurant also has outdoor seating. For those who smoke, you can sit at ground floor and take just a few steps to the outdoor area to smoke. The waiter will tend to you in a short while to give you an ash tray, which is another nice gesture, given the fact that most restaurants here are at low to mid-range.

To end, the meals were very reasonably priced. 
If you enjoy Indian food or willing to try something new then don't give this restaurant a miss.

Hello, I'm Robin, the manager of Baba's Kitchen. I was unhappy to learn about your bad experience. Our cooks rotate among our restaurants and we try to ensure that the quality and tastes are consistent, but it seems you found us on a bad day, and for that I apologize.

And as for the elevator-- yes, I agree: it is unpleasant. You clearly visited our new location, where we installed a freight elevator during construction to move the kitchen equipment upstairs. And we are now waiting for our vendor to replace the freight elevator with a smaller and much quieter dumbwaiter. We expect the new lift within a few weeks, too late to change your first impression.

Delicious food, good price, great location!
Mar 2018 • Friends
Good, cheap and cheerful Indian bang in the middle of the craziness of Bui Vien. There are two tables outside on the balcony looking down onto BV, but otherwise all are a comfortable indoors at a comfortable temperature and quiet enough to enjoy your company. Cheap Saigon beer at 25kD and good food; I particularly liked the delicious Onion Pakora, Butter Chicken and Aloo Gobi Mattar, while the Chiken Korma and samosas were tasty, but not stand-out. I liked that the condiments remained on the table throughout the meal; in my experience they generally taken away after the starters. The waiters (indeed all the staff) were running non-stop, but managed good, prompt and friendly service and it was a plus to have the water glass continuously filled with good, iced water. Book ahead if you want to go during the evening. Downstairs has a more fun atmosphere, but there is good room upstairs with very convenient power sockets by most of the tables, ideal for those of us whose phone's don't last without regular charging!

Saigon-Foody
2 contributions

Baba's Your Uncle
Aug 2017 • Friends
In a city that has recently exploded with Indian options, Baba's has remained the go-to-spot for all things Naan and Curry. While i wouldn't say it's the clear #1, it does sit in the top 3 for almost every expat that has lived in HCM. 

Obviously the standard dishes like Chicken Tikka Masala, Butter Chicken, etc., are the main staples and things they pull off really well. But do try the other extended dishes from the other regions on the menu. The Rogan Josh does seem to be inconsistent with the chunks of meat inside but when found, do offer a juicy tender mouthful. With two locations, one in D1 and another one opening in D2 (current D2 location is mainly a delivery hub), Baba's seems to be clearly focused on quality and not quantity. The portions are great although for someone with a big appetite two orders will be more than enough. I usually order two curries + naan and have enough for another full meal the next day. Despite being around a long time Baba's continues to be as consistent as the flooding in D2 after a 20 min downpour. Never change Mr. Baba, never change.

Always Superb, repeat customer
Apr 2017 • Solo
I've lived in HCMC for almost two years now, and I'm sure I echo other expats when I say that sometimes it's not easy to eat in this town. Language and cultural obstacles, availability of certain groceries - there are enough reasons to blame, including my own self. Finding vietnammm dot com and its listings of restaurants that deliver was a 'eureka!' moment for me, and there's one restaurant I use most frequently.

Baba's Kitchen isn't the first Indian cuisine I've tried in Saigon, it's just the best. Any good Indian food can claim a host of flavors and the bite of spices; Baba's is just a notch above the rest. In addition, delivery is quick and easy, correct change, the whole bit. I tip the driver above the added delivery charge, because the observant driver will then request my deliveries and we'll both benefit. Ho Chi Minh City and its businesses, as driven as they are by commerce, have a problem with selling products AND service.

Baba's Kitchen values repeat business. I had Baba's last night. today at 12 noon, my phone rang. "Hello?"

"Hello, hello! I'm sorry if I'm disturbin-"

"No, that's ok, is this Baba's Kitchen?"

It was. Naturally. They call at noon the day after I order to ask about the meal. Always. And "Bam!" Their customer service has just soared up, over, and beyond every other restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City, let alone every Indian one.

"Yes, it's Baba's. How was -"

"Baba's Kitchen, my meal was delicious, as always. Very good."

"Oh, that's good to hear, sir. Thank you very much. Goodbye."

"Thank you, Baba's Kitchen."

Yep. Funny, I've never had reason to complain about anything when they call. I wonder why?

BabaManager
Hi, I'm Robin, the manager of Baba's Kitchen. I'm sorry to learn of your disappoint and also a bit surprised. We use five different curry bases and the three curries you mention have different bases, so I would expect them to taste different. All of our chefs are from India, and we are proud that so many reviews state that our food is just like in India--but with a Southern twist, since many of our chefs are from South India.

In fact, your feelings about the naan help me understand what the problem might be. Many westerners know 'International Indian', a sweeter and saltier variant, which also features fluffy naan, rather than the flat crispy naan which is typical in India. But no matter what you were expecting, I still feel bad that you were disappointed, and if you are still in Saigon I hope you will give us another chance. Please contact me and I will make sure that we exceed your expectations--but I can't promise anything about the naan, our chefs are pretty strict about that.

We gave a review inside the restaurant too and I suggested that there wasn't enough meat on my tandoori chicken. It's described as half a chicken and I didn't get any breast meat; just 4 pieces of bones chicken that had very little (but very tasty) meat on. The waiter explained to me that they use small chickens in the tandoori so it can cook without drying out. I understand that, and it was really nice; but I still don't believe I had half a chicken (even a small one) as there was no breast meat at all, so I hope that's been taken on board.

5 stars nonetheless; the staff seem to really care about the service and food they deliver. If you like Indian food, give it a go.

Best Indian food I've ever had.
Oct 2016 • Couples
This is easily the tastiest Indian I've ever had and probably in my top 10 best meals of my life overall.

We decided to go here after reading the good trip advisor reviews and we were not disappointed. The first thing we noticed was the Indian people working and eating there, always a good indication of authenticity. On the table there were 4 little pots with different garnishes for your food, these were small pickled onions, tamarind, cool mango chutney and a (very) spicy mango garnish. When our main course arrived we were also given a freshly made mint yoghurt sauce.

Upon looking at the menu we were happy to see the cheap prices, most main courses were around 100,000 VND, roughly €4 and rice for 30,000 VND. We went here twice, I ordered the chicken jalfrezi and the chicken vindaloo (explosive spiciness but not too much to handle) and my SO had the chicken korma and butter chicken, all dishes were bursting with flavour, especially if you use all the garnishes provided. Both nights we had garlic naan on the side which was amazing, everything washed down with a cheap ice cold Saigon beer.

My other half and I shared a onion and paneer starter with popadoms and it was wonderful, chock full of ginger, garlic and fresh chilli. For mains we shared a vegetable Korma and a vegetable Vindaloo with a side of plain rice and garlic naan. Everything was exceptional, however, despite the warnings from the staff me and my boyfriend (both of us huge chilli fiends) decided that we could stomach the Vindaloo, which we categorically could not. The taste was incredible but it was like eating fire. The waiters clearly noticed our distress however because without asking brought over a large pot of Raita (a cooling yoghurt based dip), which was most welcome, accompanied by a wry smile. We also promptly ordered two mango lassies with sugar and ice, which arrived ASAP. 

As the meal came to an end our table was promptly cleared and cleaned. The waiter then brought over a small complimentary desert, a type of sweet rice pudding with cardamon. As we asked for the bill two review cards were handed to us and by filling them out we got 5% off of our bill. It was also very refreshing to see a restaurant valuing their customer experience so highly. 

All in all the service at Baba's may be some of the best I have ever received and the food was exceptional. 10 out of 10 would go again.

Definitely better than everyone else I've been to in my 4 night stay at Ho Chi Minh. But this is not to say that this restaurant was fantastic.

I would definitely return there based on the premise that I wouldn't return anywhere else I've been to.

The food was average/good. The atmosphere was brilliant, it allowed you to have a momentary slice of class and sophistication from the outside manic world of Saigon.

The one thing that stood out at Baba's kitchen was the service. I cannot fault the service whatsoever, everyone was extremely smiley, happy, and helpful. Very tentative to our needs and quick about everything. I would go back based on this fact too.

Definitely recommend going if you are staying in Ho Chi Minh!

Some good Some bad
Jul 2016 • Couples
We had some good. We had some Bad. We had dinner from Babas last night. We love Indian food and we were hopeful that this was good, because the other reviews led us to believe this. The vegetable (potato, cauliflower, pea, onion and tomatoes in dry onion sauce) was FANTASTIC. I had never eaten this dish before and I am certain to seek this out again. There was some spice to it, though I would have liked a little more, but the flavors of the onion and other spices seeped into the vegetables, tickled our mouths and delighted our taste buds and senses. The veggies were not over cooked so, you still tasted their flavors....delicious dish. On the other hand, we ordered chicken tikka masala and we were very disappointed. The dish came without spice and with a layer of 'grease' that just didn't want to mix in with the sauce in the dish. I am not sure if it was ghee or if it was some kind of oil. But, it was a flavorless masala and we won't dine on this again at Babas. The meat was okay. It is cooked in a tandoor oven, but it was seeped in the unusual, greasy and bland masala. So, no go here. The Papadams and the little packets of pickled vegetables and various other sauces, were delightful. And the naan was delicious too. There are a lot of items on this menu. And, I would not discount this restaurant just because of the masala. So, give it a try!

Has there been an Ownership Change?
Jun 2016 • Solo
As a semi regular customer (about once a month, for the past 3 yrs), I have always loved Baba's....not just for the food, which is very good, but for the service....the little touches that say you are valued & important, right up to the moment you leave the restaurant...not just until you get your food..
The checking of your satisfaction, shortly after your food has arrived....your water glass being topped up, regularly....the staff, watching eagle eyed for your slightest wish....
Small things, but ones that show that you are appreciated as a customer...
The place has always seemed to run like a well oiled machine!

For health reasons, I missed 3-4 months, & when I returned there had been changes...no familiar faces, air con, doors on the entrance...all good, not a problem!

BUT....although the food remains good, the service seems to be slipping....
The first two times I experienced this, I thought "oh well...they are very busy" & "everyone can have a bad night"...

But, last night confirmed for me that the good old days are gone....
I ordered a simple meal, & bread....it took an age to appear!
How long does it take to cook samosa, & paratha bread? In a quiet restaurant?

The samosa finally fetched up in front of me, but no bread....I started eating & was close to finishing, but still no paratha...& no sign of hovering staff...
They were all milling about socialising by the desk at the back....

I actually had to hail someones attention (unheard of at Baba's) !
If they had just forgotten the order, I could have understood it, but no, a minute or so later, the bread appeared, hot & delicious....
WTH? are the cooks only able to cook one item at a time?

No water refills...no checking of your happiness...no small discount...no interest (yanno?..."you have your food, now eat it & leave" )

I cannot eat a large amount of food at one time, & ALWAYS need a doggy bag when I leave....
One of the impressive things about Baba's, has always been , that the take away remains are always presented with the same care, as your original meal...you open it later at home, to find the remains of your meal, accompanied by small bags of pickled onions, & sauces...
No longer....you get exactly what was left on your plate, dumped in a container....

I KNOW I sound picky, & over entitled, but that is not my intention....I just hope to bring to their attention that they are on a slippery slope....
One of the key factors of the success of this restaurant, in my opinion, has been the attention to detail, the caring service that makes their guests feel welcome & content...

Without this, there is only the food...& you better make absolutely sure that this is so good,& so cheap that the lack of service & caring doesnt matter...

I do not think I will visit so regularly, any longer!

Gets better and better!
Jun 2016 • Business
My office staff selected Baba's kitchen after looking at reviews of Indian restaurants in Saigon. I have ordered from them many times in D2 and I was happy to agree that our staff lunch should go there. Once again I was totally imposed by the food quality- fast service, everything hot, fresh and delicious. If anything, I would say the food at Baba's gets better every time I eat from there. I love the little subtle things- real curry leaves in the sauces, distinct tastes ( not a generic sauce base that so many restaurants use), the right amount of heat, awesome, light, delicious naan breads and a wonderful array of colors, textures and flavours that you would not expect by looking at the restaurant from the outside. 

My only gripe is the location- I never get to that area, not being a backpacker or a middle aged single white male -so it's a long trek for most Saigon residents. Also, the facility is very basic and the staff look tired and not very enthusiastic even though the service is actually very good. I know Robin, the owner, and have done since before he opened Baba's, and I totally applaud his excellent management and outstanding food. This has to be the best consistently good Indian food in Saigon (when I order in D2, I always have a manager call me next day to check on satisfaction. This is a business that takes customer satisfaction very seriously). I would not let this spoil my review but, Robin, after all these years down in Bui Vien, I thought you might have considered a more central downtown location and a bit of a cosmetic makeover!

Best South Indian food away from home
May 2016 • Solo
I am currently travelling solo throughout Southeast Asia. During these travels the only big thing I have been missing was my parents cooking. Although we live in Switzerland, my parents are from Kerala, South India and both are great cooks, so I know how the food should taste. I chose the Southern Thali. You can choose between a vegetarian or chicken version. I went for the chicken thali. This dish is with rice and different vergetable curries, some plain sauce curries and one dish of chicken curry. The vergetable dishes get refilled free of charge, if you wish. They will come and ask you if you would like so. Everything tasted almost like at home. I have tried a few indian restaurants during my travels through Asia, but none came as close to home as this one. Very tasty.
The service staff were very polite, fast and attentive. Had a small chat with one of them, he told me that he and the cook are from Kerala, you notice it immediately through the taste of the food, that a pro is in the kitchen. The thali was spicy, perfect for me, but could be abit too spicy for some westeners.
You get free water, which they regularly fill up (also for free)
The price is reasonable I guess. Its not super cheap, but I thought it was worth it. I didnt order any drinks, but I think 28'000 Dong for a soft drink is too much, since you get them for 20'000 Dong any place else. But this restaurant is on the backpacker street, so I guess everything is abit more expensive here.

Overall I would recommend this place with no hesitation.
Keep it up :-)

We decided to check out this restaurant (around 3PM) as it was highly reviewed (over 1,600) at 4.5 stars and super close to our hotel.

Also, I want to mention that we noticed that they have been consistent, as every year from 2012 thru 2015 they were awarded the trip advisor certificate of excellence.

The staff was very attentive and polite. They smiled and refilled our water frequently. BTW, water is free! (They refill the cup thru pitchers but they have the huge gallon of bottled/filtered water in back, so drink with ease.)

We ordered a sprite, garlic naan, butter chicken, chicken fried rice, and garlic chicken. We opted for Medium spiciness, as previous reviews have mentined the spicy level can be overwhelming. Everything was wonderful and we ate it all. They even gave us some free dessert. Idk what it was, other than tasty.

Our bill was around $18 USD, such a steal for the feast we had. Back on Maui, we have maybe 1 or 2 Indian restaurants. They're quite mediocre and very expensive. 

I was so very pleased with the quality of food. I really wanted to take photos (but only realized that after inhaling our meal) I had forgotten.

If you write them a review on their in-house performance card, you'll receive 5% off. Its not much but so what, discount's a discount. 

It's so good, we're going back for dinner tonight (8-9pm) Honestly, such a gem in Ho Chi Minh city.

Also, I didn't mention this before but my boyfriend doesn't like Indian food and he's the one who asked that we go back for dinner, maybe even tomorrow. So that's gotta say something!

Delicious & friendly
Apr 2016 • Family
Walk inside this little restaurant & smell the spices of India. I love curry & have eaten curries in many different countries around the world, including India, as well as enjoying them regularly at home in London.

Baba's was certainly no disappointment & while you might argue the ethics of eating an Indian in Vietnam, it made a very welcome change to noodles. 

The staff were both very friendly & efficient, the prices very reasonable but most importantly, the food was excellent.

I had chicken vindaloo, pilau rice & aloo jeera with several saigon beers. My family don't share my love of very spicy food but the menu has all varieties of Indian food, both spicy or mild & everyone finished their dishes.

There's a comments card at the end which doesn't give you enough room to describe quite how great the food and service are. 

If you love a good curry & great service you will not be disappointed.

Very highly recommended from a Londoner that eats curry at least once a week. It's not a posh restaurant, it's a friendly restaurant with great food which are the only things I care about. 

My only disappointment is that we leave Saigon tomorrow so won't get another taste.

A disappointing experience
Apr 2016 • Couples
We had booked a table as we were expecting this restaurant to be busy - and it was. Our reservation obviously fell through the cracks as no one knew of it and we were sat upstairs at the back near the service area and toilets. It was hot and noisy and dirty. OK we thought, not a problem, the food will be good...

It was terrible. We have had some questionable curries around the world and some fantastic ones too, but this was one of the worst. 

They were both supposed to be spicy and we were warned of this and said that was fine, but neither of them were spicy at all and all we could taste was salt. The chicken curry was overcooked and the paneer jalfrezi was tasteless. I don't necessarily want a really hot spicy curry, but even a mild one should have flavour. The roti was rock hard. 

It also all came within five minutes of us ordering - including the starter along with the mains. Yet the restaurant is really small and the menu is massive so I can't believe there is a constant turnover of meals to mean that dishes are constantly on the cooker, and a rock hard roti means it wasn't recently off the hot plate I assume?

To sum up, a bad experience in a city where there is a lot of choice of venues. We have been in Vietnam for several weeks and have had some great food so I cannot recommend this restaurant in comparison.

Dec 2015 • Family
Before travelling to Vietnam we had researched restaurants on Trip Advisor and Baba's Kitchen was on our must try list. So glad we did as it was hands down our favourite Indian meal ever! Yes the restaurant is crowded and noisy and hot upstairs with just ceiling fans operating, but the friendly service and delish food make you forget all that and just go "wow!". The best I've had since I was in India!
Mar 2016
I have eaten here a few times during my stay in Ho Chi Minh, and every time it has been amazing!

Around late afternoon it is very quiet but extremely busy at other times, I would suggest trying to book a table!

The service is quick and efficient. Staff speak good English and are very helpful and friendly. 

The menu is great for vegetarians as well as meat eaters. It offers a wide selection of north and South Indian cuisine, cooked by South Indian chefs!

The food is delicious! I haven't had a curry that was so good since I was last in India 3 months ago. Everything was so flavoursome and no two dishes tasted the same! I highly recommend the dosas! I was even given rice pudding as a complimentary dessert! 

The only slight negative I have is that I was disappointed by the poppadoms. They are tiny!! And for the price I definitely expected more! 

This place is definitely not for the backpacker budget. Although currently they are offering 5% discount if you fill in a feedback form.

Overall I would highly recommend it!

There is also Free wifi available.

reviews.review_text:
websoup
San Diego, California141 contributions
0
Good Food Excellent Service with One Exception
Mar 2016 • Friends
Working in Saigon, Baba's Kitchen is one of my goto restaurant as they always serve very good authentic Indian cuisine at extremely reasonable price with excellent service. These guys take their service very seriously as evident by periodical stopover to ask about the meal as well as the survey after you asked for the bill.

Last time, I ordered delivery and they even follow-up call the next day to see if everything went well. The only hiccup is the most recent delivery experience. Not sure what happened but it was nearly 1 and half hour late.

Everyone is entitled to mistake or two. It's how you handle those mistake that says a lot about yourself. I was pretty angry by the time I got my food because of the 1 and a half hour waiting compounded by the fact that it was my first meal of the day.

To their credit, the manager called the delivery guy and instructed him to give me the food for free. Let's just say that this kind of thing will almost never happen in Vietnam. As a matter of fact, it never happened to me or my friend yet. 

So a lot of kudos to Baba's Kitchen for their ability to deal with adversity. It would have been ashamed if they didn't deal with it properly because I would likely not order again...which would be a shame because Baba's Kitchen does have some of the best authentic tasting Indian food in town.

Go NOW!
Feb 2016 • Couples
This little restaurant is in the heart of a bustling night spot. The restaurant doesn't have flashy interior but boy does it deliver EXCELLENT food and service. Boy I would swap a flashy interior for great food and service any day. There's a reason why this place has so many Tripadvisor awards. The food was really tasty and authentic Indian. We ordered two entrees. Our server was super helpful in recommending was really spicy, what was popular, and what would go well with what we'd picked so far. His suggestions were spot on. The menu has little symbols as well to help with you the many, many choices you have. I only orders the favorites and oh my goodness. They where tasty! We had an array of condiments as well, so everything is thought of. The curries come in either chicken, mutton or vegetarian. They do not serve beef. We ordered two entrees, two curries for mains, garlic naan, rice and daal. It was way too much food but for AUD$30... We where definitely not complaining. This has been or first restaurant so far on our HCMC holiday and I would happily go back every night. They also gave us complimentary rice pudding which I think everyone gets. It's a really popular pop with the young, old and in between so go check it out. Free wifi too :) 
Thanks Baba's for the awesome night!!!

Awesome.
Feb 2016 • Couples
We had a great late lunch at Baba's and enjoyed every detail of it. The staff is very attentive and you get complimentary, ice cold water all the time. The menu has cute little descriptions for a wide range of Indian dishes both vegetarian and with meat. 

We decided to go for mango lassis, paneer naan and chicken/vegetable vindaloo. At this point our very friendly waiter intervened and tried to warn us about the vindaloo as it's the spiciest dish they serve and even he, Indian himself, doesn't like it because it's too spicy. At this point I should have given in and just ordered something else but, oh well, I just needed to experience the spiciness myself. We agreed with the waiter to get it medium spicy and off he went. 

We didn't have to wait long for our lassis which were great and food arrived shortly after. Our waiter gave us some yoghurt as well as a security precaution. So I tried my medium spicy chicken vindaloo. After half a year in Asia I thought I could eat spicy food pretty well. I was wrong. Oh boy. 

I tried my best to finish the meal, using up all of the yoghurt in the process. My tongue was swollen, my eyes watering, I have never eaten anything this spicy before. Unfortunately this lead to me not being able to taste much of my chicken and the sauce, but the vegetable vindaloo (which was not as spicy) was great and the paneer naan was simply divine. While eating, our waiter came by several times to ask how we were doing haha. 

After eating they ask you to fill out a little report card about the food and the service and for doing that you even get a small discount on your bill. We ended up paying about 320,000 VND for our meal, which is of course more expensive than a street stall, but compared to the quality of the food and service more than fair. 

Definitely recommend this place, but next time I'm just listen and go for something mild instead.

Intimidating review-card process and average food
Feb 2016 • Couples
Our starter of gobi tandoori was the star of the meal - so flavoursome and tender, I cannot fault this dish in the slightest and would order it again in a heartbeat.
For main, I ordered the paneer jalfrezi which was promised to be very spicey and it came out very gelatinous and rather bland, with paneer resembling and tasting more like sloppy tofu. My partner ordered the paneer mutter and although this had slightly more taste, it too had a strange consistency and definitely didn't posses the full flavour that we were hoping for. As this was our first indian meal in a while, we still chowed down and generally enjoyed the meal. The staff even presented us with a complimentary sweet lentil dish towards the end which was a lovely touch.

The main reason for my review however, is to stress how off intimidating it was for the owner to ask us to fill in a review card whilst hovering over us, and then aggressively scrutinise the review that we gave. We ticked the boxes 'good' and 'excellent' for all aspects and merely commented on the curry not being as spicey as hoped, so such actions were completely unnecessary. When we showed our uncomfortableness at his actions, he said that he had to check with his guests how their meal was and to learn from this, but I would ask how the restaurant can establish what their guests are truly thinking if they go about their review process in such an uncomfortable way. The service up until this point was excellent and it seems such a shame that something so unnecessary could leave such a nasty taste in my mouth. 

I was prepared to give Baba's another try but after this unpleasant ending, I will not be returning.

I do not recommend Baba's kitchen. The positives: the staff is friendly, the facility is clean enough given its location. The negatives: the food. The flavors were not complex. Probably the worse dish we had was a potato dish called aloo palak. The potatoes were not stewed in the dish, instead they were boiled and thrown in when it was time to serve. This is how most of the dishes were prepared. It made for a very bland experience for a dish I tend to normally enjoy. We also had the paneer masala, which was disappointing. The paneer was cut into very very small cubes, maybe 3mm X 3mm X 3mm. These small cubes where nearly tasteless alone, and when placed in bland masala, became a huge disappointment. 
For a beverage we had a watered down version of Chana masala tea. Not only did this have barely detectable spice, it was also served with some kind of sticky film over the top that would not go away despite my best effort.
To improve, they would have to slow cook their food, allowing time for flavors to meld. 
Obviously, we would not return for future meals, and would not recommend to even the hungriest of travelers.

reviews.review_text:

Indian Spice Success
Dec 2015 • Friends
Ordered Vegetable Samosa, Naan, Chicken Vindaloo, and Vegetable Chettinad. The naan was fresh and the samosa was a slice of India with its flavored chutney sauces. The Samosa was cooked through, not microwaved which can sometimes happen at Indian places. Our server recommended toning down the spices on our food because of how extreme our selections were. Of course, we thought every Indian restaurant we’ve been to says the same thing. But I’m glad he did. 
 The spice was perfect. Hot, lasting, and a little sweat inducing on the Vindaloo. The Chettinad was a little deeper as there are vegetables as opposed to meat to soak up the flavor. The spice wasn’t unbearable where you didn’t want to eat it. Just pace yourself and soak up the rest with naan. You’ll be surprised it’s all gone at the end.
 Service was there to always help. A couple items we added because we couldn’t get enough, and they immediately responded. Tables though can get a little crowded during the lunch hours 12-2PM. If you don’t mind sharing space, it’s worth the taste of India in Saigon.

Slightly Disappointed
Dec 2015 • Couples
We turned up and it was clear that the restaurant was very busy (always a good sign). We were told there was seating available upstairs and told to go into the restaurant and up the stairs on the left. We found the stairs at the back of the restaurant next to the kitchen and where the staff were working so felt a little bit awkward walking through. When we got upstairs we were seated at a table which was already occupied and told 'We are very busy you will have to share is this OK?' At this point it wasn't exactly easy to say no so we accepted. In the end it wasn't a problem, I'm not sure what the lady already on our table thought, I hope they asked her permission before seating us, I would have liked to have been informed prior to been taken through the restaurant and upstairs that we would have been sharing. We could have booked a table for later in the evening and come back when it was quieter. 
The food was OK, my partner loved his meal and I must admit the poppadoms and naan bread were lovely along with the selection of sauces/pickles were great. I asked for my meal to be medium heat and it when it came out of was a mild curry with no heat at all. The curry itself was good I was just slightly disappointed in the flavour. 
At the end of our meal we were given comment cards to get 5% off our meal which was great. However there is no box to put your comment card into it has to be handed straight back to the staff who can then read it. This prevented me and I would imagine a number of other people from giving any negative comments or even constructive criticism.
All in all my and my partner were split between how we felt about the meal, he loved the food, I thought it was OK and it is also reasonably priced. I think what let it down was the way we were seated and then also the comment cards at the end. If you are looking for a reasonably priced Indian I would recommend but maybe go when it's quieter or book a table in advance.

Taste Of India!
Nov 2015 • Family
Towards the end of our Vietnam trip ,all our adventurous culinary bravados fizzled out and like all Desi Indians ,we marched straight into Baba's Kitchen ! 
Hallelujah!! Dosas and uttapams!!!
An extensive Menu: both South and North Indian cuisines served with smile .
What a heartwarming sight :Local Vietnamese ordering Mutton Samosas !,
Foreigners ,armed with lonely planet guides ,ordering Garlic/butter Naans!
Expat Indians coming for their weekly fix of spicy Biryani!
Free desert sampling of Kheer was comfort food for the homesick soul.
We came again for the second time, just before we were to leave for the airport . Sadly Dosas could not be made in the limited time we had. Received not only apologies from the owner but also a Free Dosa !!! High standards of service .
Highly Recommended!

Average
Nov 2015 • Couples
Had much better Indian food whilst in Vietnam. The food came out quite fast but unfortunately the dishes were not up to our expectations after reading reviews.
We ordered a chicken vindaloo and a chicken tikka masala. Unfortunately the dishes lacked the typical flavours of a vindaloo and tikka masala. The vindaloo although very spicy lacked depth of flavour, and the tikka masala didn't resemble what we know as a tikka masala. The chicken in both dishes wasn't great, pretty dry and small pieces. 
The garlic naan was okay, lots of garlic but had bigger and better naan breads elsewhere in Vietnam. 
The rice pudding desert was interesting and worth s try.
Service was ok they took orders and food was delivered quickly, but that's it. 
If you're desperate for an Indian it's ok but trust me there are far better Indians in Vietnam for a similar price.

We live in DaLat, VietNam now, come to SaiGon about every 3 months, so in the past year and a half, we have probably spent 30 days in SaiGon. Multiply the number of days by 1 and you will have the number of times we have eaten at Baba's, and, no matter how busy they are (and they DO) get busy, there is never a false step. Neither the serving staff nor the chefs are overwhelmed by dealing with large numbers of people. Their vindaloo, chicken or mutton, is in a class by itself, and they are equally good at less spicy dishes. Particular favorites of ours are the chicken hariyali, mutton palak, aloo chanh chat, chicken tandoori, and the masala kulshan. Their dosas and samosas are also wonderful. I am a retired chef/restaurant owner, and the other part of my rave relates to the quality of service here. Water glasses are constantly refilled. Emptied plates are quietly whisked away. The staff is friendly, but not obtrusive. Baba himself oversees everything, and is a delightful man who will make you feel welcome, and if you are not familiar with Indian food, he and his staff will help you and make suggestions. All in all, it is no mystery why this restaurant constantly rates in the Top 10 restaurants in SaiGon on TA. Thank you, folks. See you in January!

All things considered, best Indian restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City
Oct 2015 • Couples
I decided to write this review after my second visit to this gem of a restaurant. The first visit was very satisfactory but the second was even better, a place like this shouldn't go unnoticed.
Unless you want a fancy, dress-code-required type of restaurant, there is nothing about this place to complain about. Not top-rated to be sure, but way above average in all aspects, from variety of dishes, to the authenticity and taste of the food, to friendly and attentive service, to very reasonable pricing.
Be sure to try the set lunch, which includes almost a dozen items for about US$5! Don't let the price fools you though, everything was delicious and more than plenty for an average eater (like me!). There's even a choice of Southern or Northern style, my wife and I tried both and were equally pleased.
The most lasting impression for us though, was the extreme length to which the staff, including the gentleman who appeared to be the manager/owner, attended to our needs. Wanted mutton instead of chicken curry in the set menu? Done. Wanted Indian rice instead of jasmin rice? Done. No hesitation, no sorry-but-I-have-to-check-first, such a refreshing attitude.
For budget-minded travelers or long time resident alike, this is one address to keep in mind if you ever long for the taste of Indian cuisine in Saigon.

I used to think Ganesh was the only place to get a decent curry in HCMC, how wrong I was. Mr Singh and Baba's Kitchen are both knocking at the door to the number 1 spot. 
Don't get me wrong, its not the best curry I've ever had (but then again I have been to India several times) but its a good meal and very good value for money...and always busy which is a good sign. What is also a good sign for me is that I've actually tried different dishes here that I have never tried before because I have confidence in the food...I've opened my palette up to far more ranging experiences than normal thanks to Baba's.

Why not 5 stars?...well, I'm a little fussy and sometimes I've come across the odd piece of fatty meat in one of the curries but certainly nothing that has put me off returning time and time again and I have to admit, less fussy people than me would not have even noticed. I'm also a butter chicken fan and, to be honest, Ganesh nails butter chicken way better than the rest including Baba's...but its not too far behind.

Delivery is excellent...have ordered many times and received fast, hot food but then I live in D2 and thats where their offsite kitchen is...some distance away from their main restaurant on Bu Vien.

Give it a go...I'm sure you won't be disappointed...

A nice meal on Bui Vien
Mar 2015 • Solo
After spending the previous night stuffing myself silly on a foodie tour, my stomach was feeling a little worn out. I wanted something simple and not too spicy, almost a little bland and dry, and not too heavy. After walking the entire length of Bui Vien to see what I could find to fit the bill. I finally decided on Baba’s Kitchen, even though I felt like I was wasting a food opportunity by eating Indian rather than Vietnamese as I have a very good Indian restaurant near my home). 

The chicken tikka and paratha fit the bill perfectly - tasty and satisfying but not overly spiced or saucy/oily. I might have been tempted to try one of the curries, if my stomach had been willing. They also had a lunch time buffet available upstairs for VND 150,000 (about AU$9). Scanning what other tables had ordered, the dishes also looked appetising and the diners seemed to be enjoying them.

While it might seem a bit expensive by Vietnamese standards, I felt the prices were fairly reasonable (especially being in such a touristy area). The table water is bottled so safe to drink and the staff are courteous and efficient. Overall, a good choice if you’re looking for a change from the local food.

It's overrated
Feb 2015 • Couples
If you are a backpacker and don't have much to spend you will love this place. The food is OK, staff was OK, but the place does not have a restaurant feeling to it. 
When we arrived it was around 22.00. We weren given the menu and after a couple of minutes the waiter came and told us "If you want to eat something you must hurry up with your order. The kitchen will be closing soon, so you must hurry up". Why give us a table if the kitchen is about to close? Apart from the language and tone (which is unacceptable) the staff were friendly, so this might have been a communication issue. English is not their native language. We ordered somasa's, and some chicken tikka massala. The people claiming this to be "authentic" indian food have not tasted "authentic" indian food. Having that said, it is not bad. It's flavoured and catered for mainly foreigners and locals who may prefer it a bit saltier and sweeter. I did not like the fact we were offered water from a glass. I did not drink it, im sure the water is fine, but I like my water in Vietnam to be sealed and bottled. Also, the sauces were already on the table (like the mint yoghurt sauce). I have no idea how long they have been on the table. Could be all day (no airco and room temperatures of 25 C does not sound good for food) It also gives a bit of a "fastfood" vibe to the place. 
Although I must say the place was packed when we arrived and I noticed a lot of backpackers. Staff were friendly ( they tried ). Food was OK. It is not the best Indian in Saigon, it is not bad either. Good for backpackers. Price was a bit expensive..we paid around 280k . You can have your dinner in a proper Indian restaurant for an extra 5 - 10 dollars.

New Baba's in District 2
Dec 2014 • Friends
This purveyor of authentic Indian food has opened an outlet in District 2 meaning that any takeaway orders arrive quicker and fresher to those of us living in District 2. They are mainly set up for takeaway orders although when we turned up there to eat they did have a couple of tables set up and treated us well. There are plans to refurbish it for eating in.

A big plus point for us is the South Indian food (uttapam, dosai) as this isn't so common. These foods are best eaten fresh and don't travel well so we haven't ordered them for delivery but when we ate there the portions were generous, the sambar was good (more curry leaves would have been even better) and the batter used had a bit of the desired sourness to it. We've eaten other stuff there like daal palak, chana masala, kulcha, naan, vegetable biryani and it's all good stuff in generous amounts. The prices are currently a bit cheaper than the other Indians in D2 too. I've given it a $$ price rating in comparison with the real cheap local places where we can eat for $1 or so.

One strange thing is that although a few items like Masala Kulcha and South Indian vegetable stew are on the menu in the outlet, they are not featured on the takeaway menu, an oversight perhaps.

GOING AGAIN!!!
Nov 2014 • Couples
To cut it short, it was the kind of place where you are sad the second your plate is clean because you want more!

Situated in the hub of Bui Vien, there is plenty of competition from other restaurants. However, walking past and seeing the tables full is a good sign of the quality that was to come. The menu has the usual range of (well priced) Indian cuisine, alongside a lot of dishes that were new to me. We ordered poppadoms, which I recommend so you can sample the home made sauces (the mint one in particular was divine) and to follow I went for my usual favourite of butter chicken. I wish I hadn't, not because it wasn't delicious but because the chefs clearly know what they are doing so I could have been more experimental! The flavours were explosive and the portion size was spot on. The naan breads are huge, we shared one and one rice between us (and we are pretty big eaters!) If you like your garlic then get the garlic naan, but you have to really love it as the load of garlic is extremely generous. The meal is then followed by a complimentary rice pudding dessert which cleansed the pallet of the mild aftermath of spices. 

The service was INCREDIBLE! Normally, we tip out of obligation but this is the kind of restaurant where you don't question the fact the waiters deserve it. They kept our glasses of water topped up so it was constantly chilled, the owner swept around the guests regularly and the general vibe from the staff was that they genuinely love what they do!

Could not recommend it much more if I tried!!!

Best service I had in Vietnam as well as some of the best Indian food I've ever had
Sep 2014 • Solo
I went to several Indian restaurants in Saigon and this one is hands down the best. I originally ate there on recommendation of a friend and it quickly became one of my favorite restaurants in town. In about a month I went there more than ten times. The staff is very attentive. The best service I've received in Vietnam. They consistently refilled my water and always asked how my food was. This type of service seems very rare in this "backpacker" part of the city. The norm is more touristy restaurants who are not counting on repeat business and you can guess the result.

Every meal I had at Baba's was beyond delicious. They will make it to your spice level and the chefs have good recommendations if you ask them. My favorites were the chicken tikka masala and the mushroom shrimp curry. Every time I went there I had a waiter who spoke very good English too.

The lunch specials allow you to try different types of curries. There are a variety of different types of delicious naan bread. Every table has some pickled onions, tamarind and mint sauces as well as another more spicy selection. The onions were especially delicious.

 I also highly recommend the buffet on Saturdays.

Only Indian food for novices, much much better in HCMC at same price
Jul 2014 • Business
First off, you have to realize this is located in backpacker paradise area of HCMC. I would suspect that the people that think this place is excellent Indian food have never eaten any GOOD Indian food. The place is a dump, the person that waited on us was an arrogant Punjabi Indian, which having a real Indian person with us, dd not impress. the food was as expensive as eating at Ganesh, but without the ambiance, or anything else. Kitchen the size of a phone booth. We tried chili Paneer, and after eating the same at Ganesh and Tandoor this trip, this was plain, and without spice and without any presentation at all. Come on, having nothing but waterspots on the table top is disconcerting, it is a dump. After a few starters, and after having eaten at Ganesh the night before, and Tandoor the night before that, we left and went back to Ganesh to finish eating. Granted you might want to be clean and presentable to go to Ganesh, but you don't need to put on a suit or tie, but once you eat at Ganesh or Tandoor, you would certainly turn your back on this place. The water boy was indeed friendly and smiling, but can't make up for mediocre cook and surly waiter. Food was good only if you've never eaten real Indian food before. I've been to India, and Kuala Lumpur which has a very good Indian restaurant, and well as Gaylord in Hong Kong, several years ago. Consider this place your introduction to Indian food if you've never eaten Indian food before, then try better places. Ganesh and Tandoor aren't any more expensive, and are real restaurants. This dump is living off ratings of unknowing people thinking it is good.

Baba's Kitchen or Ganesh?
May 2014 • Friends
My favourite Indian restaurants in HCMC are Baba's Kitchen on Bui Vien Street and Ganesh on Hai Ba Trung. Which is better?
Well, if you judge the two restaurants purely on their best dishes, Ganesh is the winner. For example, the non-vegetarian thali, served with lamb, for 165,000 VND is a superb dish, better than anything at Baba's.
If you factor in price, then Baba's is cheaper - e.g. 125,000 VND for a non-veg thali. 
If you go by atmosphere, Baba's is very informal and open to the street, whereas Ganesh is plusher, an air-conditioned box shut off from the noise and traffic outside. 
If it's fish you're after, then Baba's is the winner. Baba's uses barramundi fish in its curries, which is superior to the basa fish used by Ganesh.
And then there is the 'mine host' factor. Ganesh is fairly impersonal, whereas Robin, the owner of Baba's, is friendly and helpful and always ready to talk about his beloved Manchester United!
I will continue to use both restaurants.

Service was mediocre this time, and terrible last time. A $0.35 Coke costs $1.40, The service water tastes odd, perhaps because they serve it in a metallic cup, and the cups are oddly small.

London, United Kingdom70 contributions

Superb food from a curry addict
May 2014 • Friends
Had an amazing meal at Baba's, very much a western style India orinated menu and you can find familar dishes as those offered by UK and Australia restaurants.

After reading some of the less favourable reviews and someone who has cooked British Indian Resturant cuisine for many years, I was a little hesitant, but in short it was an excellent meal. It makes me wonder why they receive some contrasting reviews, a chef having an off day?

On ordering my food I was offered a choice of how I wanted the dishes to arrive based on my selection, which ended up being timed perfectly. 

I started with roasted poppadom with Masala. This came with four individual chutneys, all fresh and full of flavour and a superbly spiced bowl of Masala. However, what I didn't realise was there would be only one poppadom which wasn't enough for all the aforementioned condiments, apparently if ordered fried, you get two for the same price.

Chicken Tikka was perfect, good flavour and not dry, Chicken Jalfrezi had excellent spice levels, large serving and used less oil than in typical western versions. Garlic Naan was thin, crispy and well cooked. 

I tried to order rice off menu, asking for Keema Pilau but was told the chef couldn't accommodate my request, however when the dish arrived, I did surprisingly get my request. It was great and more like a mutton biriyani, with nice pieces of soft meat.

It is relatively a compact outfit which is split over two floors, the upper having two tables on an outside terrace overlooking the street plus air-conditioning. It's certainly not priced or pretending to be a fine dinning establishment but offers great food at reasonable prices.

The resturant was full when I arrived and people waiting outside, however there were some folks who hogged tables for a few hours and had finished eating before I arrived and continued to consumed the free water after I'd left.

OK, the Baba's is in the backpacker area, but this small restaurant needs to turn covers and if you visit and it's busy, perhaps consider the other people who maybe waiting to dine and the restaurants balance sheet.

Totally recommended, great food and service and certainly deserves the high rating it holds on TA

A varied menu made it difficult to chose; eventually, we settled on a fish tandoori, chicken kadhai, garlic naan and vegetable rice. Everything was seasoned & cooked beautifully. With the bill came a comment card, and the service team were very appreciate of any and all feedback.

BabaManager
I was disappointed to learn of your experience at Baba's. While we hope to please every customer, we also understand that people have different tastes. I believe the reviews here and elsewhere show that Baba's offers the authentic flavors of India, both Northern & Southern dishes. We do meet a few customers who believe they know Indian food when in fact they have only eaten "International" Indian. The international indian taste is sweeter, saltier, less spicy, less flavorful, and sometimes even contains MSG! These customers often complain that our food is different from their experience. All I can do is encourage them to try something new, real Indian cooking. As you note, there are other Indian restaurants and many of them offer the international Indian taste. I certainly don't fault your preference, because any Indian food--even the international taste--is better than no Indian food! I hope you will give us another chance, but I respect your decision in any case. Thanks for the feedback.

reviews.review_text:
Philip M
Maclean, Australia16 contributions
0
Beware of the vindaloo!
Oct 2013 • Couples
Last evening my wife and me visited Baba's kitchen after checking the reviews on tripAdvisor. The restaurant is medium sized and we got a friendly greeting from the restaurant staff and chilled water was soon delivered to our table, which was just perfect on a sultry evening.

We ordered mutton samosas to kick off the meal. They arrived hot and had a pleasant aroma, the shortcrust pastry was crisp and can be recommended.

So on to the main course, which turned up just as we were finishing eating the samosas, I'm not sure whether that was either good or bad as some people like a rest between courses. 
My wife ordered the mutton rogan josh (medium) and that's how it was served as well as being flavoursome and slightly above average.
I went for the mutton vindaloo and the waiter did warn me it was very spicy, which I expect for any vindaloo. As a seasoned curry muncher for many decades I appreciate a hot curry and recognise the hottest variety are known as a phall, which is too hot for me and the vindaloo was indeed a phall strength dish, so hot in fact I was unable to cope. The very responsive waiter could see that I was having difficulty coping with it and promptly delivered a saucer of raita to soothe things a bit and the chilled water kept flowing - even so I could only manage to eat part of it. The waiter was very polite and understanding, he was apologising profusely and was disappointed for me. I partly blame myself as had been somewhat pre-warned.

We also had the keema naan as a side and that was nice, but have to add it had the thinnest layer of mince that I've ever seen in a keema, but the portion size was reasonable.
The plain rice was just a basic long grain variety and fluffy as opposed to the more traditional basmati you expect to recieve in an Indian food establishment. Perhaps basmati isn't widely available in Saigon?
It has to be said the meal accompaniments were good.

So apart from the very fiery vindaloo, I can see why this restaurant gets good reviews as we found the service and staff attentiveness top notch, the food was very good if not quite excellent and we intend going back next week to try something else. I'll add to this review after.

One slight detraction was the restaurant is open to the street and the incessant bibbing and honking from the passing traffic was irritating. Being open to the street there is no air-conditioning.

Made Onam Great!
Sep 2013 • Friends
Onam may be a one-day celebration for Malayalee Community and near to them in Saigon, but the Taste of Onam sadhya spread out by Baba's Kitchen is lasting longer than that..Its taste still linger around..
The lunch was served on a banana leaf in the traditional Kerala style..Starting from the pickles, including sweet and tangy pickles made from lemon, mango and ginger, followed by the all-time favorite crispy banana chips—both sweet and salty and Kerala papadams.
This was followed by the Thoducurries (Minor Curries) — Kalan, Olan, Erisserri, Pachadi, Thoran and so on were served ..The volunteers who served filled my leaf by this time, by their over sized serving spoons…
I have to really make space in leaf for the Rice and sambhar, Wish I had a bigger leaf..Main Curries such as Sambar, Aviyal and Rasam were so true to the original, many can’t resist multiple helpings…
The payasams, Palada Pradhaman and Parippu Payasam tasted so good, I never tasted something as good! 
I wish Baba's Kitchen organize this Keralite Vegetarian Sadhya often at their restaurant as a regular feature, I will be first to join that!

as a typical Indian soul-at-heart person, I had Indian food cravings only on the second day of my trip to Vietnam & chanced upon this restaurant as it is only a few doors away from the hotel I was staying at...& it did not disappoint. After my order of dhal palaak didn't come through, the staff offered to exchange the curry (had palak paneer instead), but still delivered dhal palak at no extra charge. I felt bad about wasting the food though, but the staffs offered to pack the leftovers for me- but as we were traveling out from the city I declined. I do hope that the food did not go to waste. the masala kul cha that I had with my palak paneer was yummy- all gooey and crispy and filled with goodies- all one wanted from a naan. the portions are big enough to share among two people, and each order comes with a selection of sides (chutney, pickled onions, a sweet sauce, and pickled mango) and desserts (a sweet porridge thing); at no extra charge. You'd also get a 5% discount if you fill in the review. Our first visit was so good that when we arrived again n Saigon for the last leg of our trio post-6-hours bus ride on only breakfast- we went straight to thus restaurant again and satisfied ourselves with Beriyani, both of us were able to finish a dish each this time as we were famished, but the flavour of the dishes were not discounted and the service was top notch as usual. Jul 2013 • Couples
This little indian place located in the heart of HCMCs backpacker district offers staples from both South Indian and North Indian cuisine. We were lured in by a brit sitting in the front of the restaurant obviously enjoying his food tremendously, and were not dissapointed. Our lunch consisted of a paneer butter masala, that had nicely balanced flavours of coriander and chili + wonderful richness in the gravy: the richness might of been from milk or cream blended with some cashews but that is anyones guess. We also had some garlic naan that was appropriately chewy but not as fluffy as expected & a masala dosa that came with an ocra curry ( who doesn' t love ocra?) with subtle flavours of jeera an chili, a wonderful tomato based sauce and a cooling coconut curd. The dosa was crispy and the potato filling had just enough mustard seeds to create a nice sensation in the mouth. Our only complaint was, that the dishes came at a very different times - that seems to happen a lot in HCMC and the waiters were v. apologetic- my husband had finished his food when mine finally came. All and all Babas kitchen was a a very positive experience and offered good value for money.

No need to sample the competition
May 2013 • Family
We have resided in HCMC for two plus years. During this time we have sampled all of the Indian restaurants and Babas wins hands down. We eat in, or order takeaways once a week.
The owner, Robin, is always on-site overseeing his competent staff.
The meals are cheap and are delivered quickly. Wine and beer is available equally inexpensively. Should downstairs appear full, there is an upstairs area including two tables outdoors overlooking the interesting street of Bui Vien.
If your accommodation is in the area of the Caravelle, Park Hyatt, Intercontinental, Grand etc, you only have a ten minute cab journey costing a couple of dollars in order to get there.
Preferring veg food, our favourite dishes include both yellow and black dhal, aloo jeera and aloo ghobi. Chicken hyderabad is also stunning. There is a large choice of naan.
A Tip. If you like a hot curry, order medium at Babas. Flavoursome and perfect.

BabaManager
I was horrified to learn of your experience at Baba's. When I saw your review on Tripadvisor, I searched the comment cards and found yours. I then rang the phone number on it and, as you recall, we discussed your stomach troubles. While it is not impossible that the rasam soup made you sick, I must confess to a bit of skepticism. Rasam soup is simply spices and tamarind, there's nothing that could bring about the distress you suffered. I note that you did have vindaloo chicken--spicy, as you ordered it. Perhaps you had a bad dish, or a reaction to the chili, or maybe it was just too spicy?

I'm very sorry you suffered so, and I want to make it up to you. I hope you will contact me on your next visit to Saigon and I will make things right. And be assured the staff and I are reviewing our processes in response to your unhappiness.

Nice venue, superb Indian food and excellent service
Feb 2013 • Friends
The ambience created by Baba's smart choice of colour and artificial lighting was superb. Members of their staff were efficient. Several small tables were pulled together quickly to form a larger table upstairs which gave us plenty of space and excellent ventilation for all nine of us under the fans. There were many customers but we did not feel uncomfortable with our seating upstairs. The dishes arrived with very good presentation, flavour and taste. The chefs were clearly experts in traditional Indian cooking. We found that the combination of foods was excellent, having taken a few recommendations of the very friendly waiter who took our order. We specified that we liked more beans in the vegetarian korma and it arrived with the right proportion of beans cooked with the right timing. The green curry was exceptionally good. All dishes were very well received by every one and the quantity was just right. The food quality was great and there was nothing that we did not like. Even the one who had no preference for spicy dishes enjoyed the meal. The bill was very reasonable, at US$7 per person net. There was no extravagant decoration or fancy furniture and the management minimized waste of time and floor space which probably accounted for the reasonable prices for patrons. This restaurant could still made a profit because of the volume of business due to its reputation!

Tasty food and commendable service
Feb 2013
In the month and a half we've spent in SE Asia, we haven't had a single restaurant meal featuring good service -- except at Baba's. It might be a cultural preference in SE Asia, but it's often difficult to get a waiter's attention after the initial order. They just disappear. At Baba's, the manager/owner was personally directing "traffic," and our water glasses never went empty. We were provided with a full set of silverware (and several napkins -- hooray!) and the waiter took the time to explain all the chutneys. Our food was prompt and delicious. Dessert, a type of rice pudding, was complimentary -- and complementary! We received our check right after we requested it, and it came with a questionnaire offering 5% off the bill if we rated the service and food (on the questionnaire card -- not TripAdvisor).

If you seek delicious, authentic Indian food at fair prices, I would definitely recommend Baba's. The service can't be beat!

Varied menu, delicious food, great service
Feb 2013 • Solo
I had one of my best meals in Ho Chi Minh City at Baba's Kitchen on Bui Vien. On one of my visits there (I went twice) I was in the mood for snacks rather than a meal so I ordered veggie bhajis and chicken samosas. Both were delicious, and were even better when dipped in one of the home-made spicy and sweet sauces provided. On another visit I had chicken biryani. You are always asked what spice level you want. I asked for spicy, and I wasn't disappointed! My only complaint - and this was common for most restaurants in Ho Chi Minh City - is that the chicken was dry. The portions at Baba's Kitchen are generous, but the nice thing is that the staff will wrap up your leftovers if you want. 

The staff are particularly attentive at Baba's. The Indian owners always stop by to chat and to make sure you are happy with the food. The Vietnamese servers are quick and efficient. And, in one of my visits, I noticed that the staff happily swapped ingredients for a client who either had celiac disease or dairy intolerance. So, if you need special service, go to Baba's!

Best Indian in the Backpacker Area
Jan 2013 • Solo
I've been eating here since it opened, and a few times a week at that. Needless to say, I love the food here, and the staff are generally excellent by local standards. I've never had any health problems that I could connect with the food here either, so given I've probably eaten over 100 meals here I'd say that counts for "sanitary food".

So, the food: like I said it's the uncontested champion of the Bui Vien/Pham area in my 2.5 years of eating experience here. Other places do certain dishes better, but they lack the location, service standards, and in some cases low prices of Baba's. The food tends to be on the spicy side as well, though they can tone it down upon request. My only real complaint is that the chicken tends to be too chewy/dry in the curry dishes like jalfrezi, but when done alone as a tikka it's usually much softer and juicier. The quality is highly consistent.

The service is excellent by local standards. The staff are clearly very concerned about customer satisfaction and enjoyment, and the servers are usually quite attentive. The people who take your order and manage the restaurant have a high level of English fluency as well.

Delivery times are usually good (usually ~30min to D5 at 8-9PM) with the food in good condition and still hot.

The atmosphere could be improved, though. It's not bad, but it's not great either - again, there are better places in the city for that, but in the backpacker district it's probably one of the best still. Sort of a standard, informal restaurant with fairly low-key Indian music (which in itself is a nice plus, in my opinion). I would suggest eating on the second floor to avoid the street noise. Otherwise, the restaurant is clean with a decent restroom and a lack of pests. Not a place to meet people, just to talk to ones you've already met.

Prices are fairly low: $ 75-100,000VND for a typical main dish, 30-50 for rice, about 20-40 for naan, and drink prices all appropriate for the area norm.

Overall, a nice place to frequent for lunch or dinner alone or with friends. Highly recommended for a low-price, high-quality meal.

A cheery Indian food place
Dec 2012 • Family
Have been here 3 times now - twice in the evening and once for lunch. Despite the very ordinary and basic decor, furnishings and facilities (in line with many places on Bui Vien Street), this is a nice spot to have a meal. What makes the restaurant better than the many other Indian restaurants in the area is the warm welcome and attentiveness of the Tamil manager (and other staff). And the food is good as well.

Here are some of the really good dishes here: Chettinad chicken (curry): very spicy, excellent; vegetable korma: mild but delicious, with the vegetables not over-cooked; tandoori chicken: the half tandoori has four large pieces of succulent chicken on a kind of salad. These last 2 dishes are good for people who don't like spicy food. The rice and the various breads are fine as well - the parathas being perhaps the best of the breads. 

Most people seem to eat downstairs, whereas the best place to eat is perhaps on the balcony of the first floor room, from where you have a good view of the street.

It's always a good sign when you mentally plan to go back to a restaurant at the end of a meal there. This is the case with Baba's Kitchen - for me at least. 

This restaurant is warmly recommended (for those who are modest in their demand for comfort).

Brilliant value, service and food
Jun 2012 • Couples
Baba's Kitchen serves up delicious North and South Indian food in an unpretentious restaurant in the Backpacker area. Vegetarians are well catered for and all meat is Halal It. 's easy to find, situated across the street from Stella/Stellar cafe and between a barber shop and a dress shop called FUKI.
Expect an open to the street restaurant, there are plenty of fans and there is an A/C section upstairs. Cold water served immediately and continuously and one of the best written Indian menus I've come across. 
There are two things which set Baba's Kitchen apart from the host of other Indian eateries in HCMC,food and customer service. Food is consistently good, I know this as I've been eating here or at Robin's previous joint, Mumtaz, for five years, Portions are generous and you have the option of asking for food to be spiced up or down. Customer service is taken seriously, whether you're just passing through or a regular your opinions are sought and paid attention to. 
It's not the fanciest of Indian restaurants in HCMC but it's pleasant and comfy and if you're looking for home style Indian cooking and a friendly atmosphere at very decent prices it's the only place to go.

BabaManager
Hello! I'm sad to learn you were unhappy with your experience at Baba's, and I think a few points need clarification.

You visited Baba's during the week of Tet, an annual week-long celebration during which many Vietnamese return to their hometowns. As in many other restaurants, our entire Vietnamese staff was on holiday, and so Baba's was only open for a few hours each night, serving dinner with a reduced menu. We did not serve South Indian food during Tet because we lacked the staff to cook both North and South Indian dishes. While our cooks are Indian, our Vietnamese kitchen staff helps with ingredient preparation. North & South dishes are very different and both are very labor intensive, and we opted to serve the more popular of the two. Again, I apologize for your disappointment and assure you that we'll have our South Indian dishes when you return! 

Second, you state that Baba's uses "Vietnamese rice," which is simply not true; like other Indian restaurants in Vietnam, we use jasmine rice from Thailand. Further, I'd like to point out that we serve Uppuma every day, and vada (along with idli) on Tuesday. Our vada and idli are fresh; we refuse to serve frozen pre-made items.

As for any confusion while ordering a vegetarian korma, I can assure you that many of our regular customers are vegetarian, and we have many vegetarian options on the menu. I can only apologize for the confusion and remind our staff to clearly communicate with our customers, even during busy times such as Tet dinner.

I'm very pleased to learn that you intend to visit us again; our South Indian dishes are waiting for you, and I hope the above clarifications put your mind at ease. I strongly believe that our reviews here and elsewhere reflect our commitment to great food and service at a reasonable price!

Very clean, great food. Fantastic service
Dec 2011
Just got back to the hotel so I thought I'd put this up while it's fresh. Our family is 2 adults and an 8yo girl.
VALUE - We went vegetarian and had the Veg korma, eggplant masala, daal, 1 plain rice, 2 naan breads a beer and a Coke. Total cost 260,000 Dong. About $13 So let's tick the value for money box to start with.
CLEANLINESS - Look we all know good food and clean premises don't always go hand in hand in Vietnam. There are some Indian places down an alley off Pham Ngu Lau that just look downright scary. Baba's isn't like that at all, they obviously take pride in providing a clean place to eat.

THE FOOD - OK, so onto the business end now. The food was great! We ordered all vegetarian, and because we had a kid with us, we ordered everything mild. So we had a bit of a handicap to begin with. But Baba's delivered with nice flavoursome dishes, and ample quantity. One small crit, the cheese naan was burnt, it had a burnt cheese taste. But seriously imo cheese naan should only be ordered in a Westfields Foodcourt at lunchtime. It doesn't go with proper Indian food (we ordered it for the kid). There was also an assortment of accompaniments which were topped up as we ate (Mango Chutney WINs)
SERVICE - Finally the service was excellent. We had some questions over items in the menu, which the staff were able to answer, and they also made good suggestions on what to order. During the meal we had 2 staff members come and ask us if everything was in good order.
Lastly we were given feedback surveys at the end of the meal (Continuous Improvement, great way to run a business) which entitled us to a 10% discount.
Oh, and a Christmas card from Baba's as we left :)

Thoroughly recommend!!

ローランド

Good, solid, satisfying Indian food
Nov 2011
After eating a fair amount of Indian food in the States (LA, SF, Boston), I generally categorize the (Northern) Indian food that you get in America in two categories: generic (think buffet style) and gourmet. Compare to the "gourmet" style Indian restaurants I've been to, Baba's Kitchen is definitely up there among the best.

I ordered the Vegetable Pulao rice which was decent--not sure if they used basmati rice here, but it was still good. I also had an order of the garlic naan which wasn't quite as fluffy as I'm used to, and while you could certainly see the chunks of diced garlic, it didn't taste as garlicky as it could have been. 

But it was really the Lamb Vindaloo that made this meal. I eat pretty spicy, so most vindaloos in the US aren't spicy enough for me, but this was the perfect spice level (Americans beware!). Also a lot of lamb that I've eaten in Vietnam tends to be overcooked and too chewy (e.g. Au Parc), but Baba's gets it right--not the best cut of lamb in the world, but I wasn't complaining. Potatoes cooked perfectly too--not so much that they turned to mush like in some Indian places I've been.

The other thing that I really enjoyed were the chutneys and pickles that came with the meal. I usually have a hard time with these, but these pickles were the perfect blend of salty and sour and the chutneys were not overly sweet like they sometimes are.

All told: 150,000 VND with the 10% discount for filling out the comment card. Wait staff very attentive and good with recommendations. I'll definitely be coming back here next time the Indian food craving strikes.

I am ecstatic... through recommendations from fellow Indian food lovers a group of us ventured to Bui Vien Street in the bustling backpacker area of Saigon to sample some Indian cuisine. 
I was curious as I heard that Robin, the former manager of Mumtaz, a restaurant that had become a firm favourite of mine had decided to venture out on his own and open BaBas Kitchen just down the street from Mumtaz.

Robin has lifted quality and affordable Indian food to a new level.

The service was courteous and attentative despite the restaurant being packed for midweek lunch. And the beer was COLD!
The restaurant was comfortable and offered a happy ambience. A good indicator of the respect any establishment has for its customers is the standard of the restrooms.... Babas Kitchen has a well appointed and clean restroom.

All my companions agreed that Babas Kitchen will become an institution and a favourite for locals and tourists alike.
